explanation: Plants exhibit an alternation of generations, cycling between diploid (2n) and haploid (1n) stages. The haploid spore is created by meiosis and germinates into the gametophyte stage, which produces gametes. When these gametes fuse, they form a diploid (2n) zygote that grows through mitosis into the sporophyte stage. The sporophyte then produces spores to repeat the cycle. As plants became better adapted to life on land, the sporophyte stage became the dominant phase of their life cycle.
